Figure 1:Motivation and overview of MMMem.(a) Without task-level memory, the evidence for a question stays scattered across records, and the agent can repeat mistakes on related questions.
(b) MMMem organizes multimodal memory, generates tasks for warm-up and training, turns solved tasks into experiences, and retrieves and reuses them on later tasks.

Figure 2:MMMem framework.(a) Each memory node holds text, image, page, and generated views of its source records.
(b) Tasks generated from the source memory are used to train the reader offline and to warm up the memory.
(c) For the current question, text and image retrieval followed by reranking selects the evidence. The agent answers with its sources, writes a note, and may generate an image; the resulting experience moves from staged to retained after repeated, source-supported reuse.

Figure 3:Case studies of MMMem.(a) A generated view combines clues from multiple records for visual retrieval and bird identification. (b) A recalled experience links the common and scientific names of a bird in a photo-counting task. (c) The task warm-up example compares answers to a dog-breed question with and without warm-up.
